* I expect mathematical proofs hard to be likely proved by 2050.
* I expect P vs NP and maybe also the Navier-Stokes problem will be proved by 2040.
* The Yang-Mills problem has more physiological issues than theoretical ones, but turns out to be related to the other of the Millennium Prizes. I expect it to be solved around 2050 as well, if then.
* The Riemann Hypothesis is easily the most complex Millennium Prize Problem, but since the is no Famous Physicist among the mathematicians that tried to to solve it, it was left partially open till now, I expect it to be proved also around 2050 by a mathematician, maybe not a Fields Medalist, something that I expect to prove it, as 2017 have been the barren fields of a once Fields Medalist, now without a job.
* The Conjecture of Birckh and Swinnerton-Dyer. Although recent progress has been made in recent years by some aforementioned mathematicians, the problem has decades behind in that research, I expect between 2030 and 2050 for people to work on that, once they have a better context of it's structure, some heuristics to attack it. But, a proof will happen after that, and maybe even a conjecture about solving it's heuristic as Artin Conjecture, have it's suitable generalization as an extension of the ${\displaystyle x^{p}=1}$ equation.

Decomposing into several smaller questions, most likely combination of the algorithmic problems, like Navier Stokes, they will be proved by 2040. Yang Mills and the Riemann Hypothesis has more I dont know what(not publicly, at least) mathematicans to research it, or, put it differently, the complexity of those, although the same could be said of the other contested problems, will be proved after that, and most likely in less than 10 years from their actual solution, so, depending on who proves it, sometime between 2049 to 2050 in the best case scenario. The research of the Birch and Swinneton-Dyer problem is too stagnated for it to be their for a while, but for is complexity to take it more than 100 years to be proved. I expect rather at 2030 for the greatest barrier to the conception of solving the problem to be crossed, and by no means will the problem be solved in less than a 10 year span, if it this ever happens.

The key points to this are that there are almost none mathematicians actively researching the following problems, including at least one non professor and another non-academic researcher, and all that have tried to prove it have fallen on their knees with the adversary of it. Pregnant by this and the knowledge of the best mathematicians in the world, like CMI, to put a deadline of 9 years for their solution, which is a short timespan to tackle Millennium problems, I have a 0% chance they are solved those 9 years, and even if they are, it is supported also by the way the university system works in Europe (and probably the rest of the world). Not only trial by error and good intuition are not punished by the slowly arriving salary at younger ages to earn living as mathematician, but earning no living until we earn our first achievement as PhD or postdoc is a way of punishing us, so u have to be very patient to get paid. Even in other Universities like Zürich or Cambridge with more presteady Hardship, there is a possibility for lack of living, methods of trial and error can imply a loss of time and money to solve a problem.

Besides that, I have a good guess at the type of problem that is to be solved. I expect any of the three fluid problems to be proved very quickly by an AI, and the one on Prime Numbers at the most difficult, but supported by theoretical results around 2025 if not before, to be solved by a scholar very possibly not a Fields Medalist. Also I expect the problem on Prime Numbers extended to complex solution space to be proved with the exact same steps in 2030 or 2040, by no possible means will it exceed 100 years. Lastly i expect the problem of P vs NP and the Riemann Hypothesis to be proven. Due to atleast one Professor that have taken this research from a dead end to a future probable solution by 2035 but no later that 2045, with the exact same research strategy, and the P vs NP problem to be eventually solved. 
It is interesting to note something about the Commonweath of Mathematicians, even given the lack of funds, it is common between most fields, like Math, the Physics, the Computer Science, to get back to the old school theory of Knowledge that has come and gone with that of Scientism, who has reduced the human knowledge to a set of exact laws and methods, where we would lose all of our social connections, and especially the explanation of biological phenomena.

With no valid explanation to human biological phenomena (the evolution of, nature of life and consciousness, or even the presence of the earth inside the solar system) it has be reduced to what people put into the fields of the Art and the the Nature, our own professors (their scientific methods are not sufficient at any moment of investigation), all our life is math, its pillars are mere tweedelium and tweed- loom!

Forecast date: 2024-09-19. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Assign a probability to the event occurring on or before each of the listed deadlines. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.
